newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania considers oil blocks tender deadline.
newsitem.headline: Romania considers oil blocks tender deadline.

text.p: Romania's National Agency for Mineral Resources (ANRM) is considering plans to postpone a deadline this month on a tender for 15 onshore and offshore oil blocks, a senior ANRM official said on Wednesday.

"We've received a series of requests from companies which bought our tender documents to postpone the deadline to submit their offers for the tender," Secretary of State Doru Badulescu, head of the ANRM, told a news conference.
"They said they need more time to study the data in the documents."

In April, the ANRM put up for tender nine prospective oil blocks chain-linked along the eastern rim of the Carpathians, plus two near the northern border with Hungary and Ukraine, two in southern Romania and two on the Black Sea continental shelf.
It set October 31 as deadline for potential bidders.
"We are studying those requests and will decide soon whether to postpone or maintain the deadline," Badulescu said. "However, a new deadline would mean anything between two to six months from now."
Badulescu said 47 Romanian and foreign oil companies and consortia had bought the tender documents. He refused to identify the bidders.
"At this stage, all I can say is that U.S. oil companies have bought most of the data packages," Badulescu said.
Romania needs capital and modern technology to discover oil deposits in deep or difficult structures. Local oil companies can drill only to depths of 4,000 metres.
Agency sources told Reuters recently that potential winners in the tender would invest a minimum $30 million and be able to drill at depths exceeding 4,000 metres.
Technology transfer and training programmes were additional assets for a successful bidder, the sources also said.
Seeking an increase in oil output in 1991, Romania offered concessions to firms including Royal/Dutch Shell Group, Enterprise Oil Plc and Amoco Corp.

The Balkan country is a mature oil and gas producing region. But frenzied exploitation of reserves under the former communists and poor equipment led to a decline in crude oil output over the past 20 years.
Crude production was around 6.7 million tonnes (equivalent to about 134,000 barrels per day) last year, compared to a peak of 14.7 million tonnes (some 294,000 bpd) in 1986.

Under a new petroleum law, Romania puts local and foreign investors on equal footing. The law covers concessions, taxes and royalties and includes a one-year profit tax exemption following the start-up of production.
